hypothesis: Closing an open ETH lifecycle at the next one-minute open after a fresh completed-five-minute BREAKOUT onset whose point-in-time breakout direction opposes the position will improve the unchanged native 60-bps-stop and 12-hour-fallback exit after fees, slippage, and official funding.
decision: Reject this exact opposing-breakout exit for live or observer promotion. It was technically causal and preserved all 282 development and 56 opened-final entries, but it reduced development net return by 137.395649 bps, improved only two of five chronological folds, and still lagged development control by 38.163928 bps under the one-minute delay stress. The opened-final headline improved by 65.009888 bps, but maximum drawdown worsened, net return excluding the largest winner remained negative, and the short slice remained negative. Keep V58 runtime unchanged and do not retune this trigger on the already-opened windows.
falsifier: Update this rejection only if a source-bound implementation audit finds an entry-parity, completed-bar timing, breakout-direction, funding, fee, slippage, or stop-precedence defect, or if genuinely future source-compatible lifecycles contradict the historical result. Parameter retuning on these opened windows does not falsify it.

evidence.role: outcome-blind frozen hypothesis and success contract
source-bound causal replay with exact trades, folds, sides, and delay stress
prior rejected global R5 profit-lock family
frozen official hourly Hyperliquid funding input
immutable V58 live prefix containing the motivating resolved ETH path

limitations: The hypothesis was motivated after observing one selected V58 ETH giveback path.
The opened-final 60-day block had already been viewed in prior ETH research and is not prospectively unseen.
One-minute OHLCV cannot reproduce private IOC latency or exact sub-bar ordering.
The replay models completed five-minute state projected onto one-minute rows; implementation parity does not prove future market efficacy.
The rejection applies to this exact unconditional opposing-breakout exit and does not establish that every distinct exit mechanism is ineffective.
